deities: Devi Kanya Kumari (Parvati in virgin form)

history.dynasty: Ancient (legendary; Travancore kingdom in later history)
history.period: Mentioned in Ramayana, Mahabharata, Yajurveda, Sangam works (Manimekalai, Purananuru) and the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea (60-80 CE)
history.summary: Dedicated to Devi Kanya Kumari, the virgin (kanya) form of Parvati, who slew the demon Banasura — he could be killed only by a virgin. Sage Narada (as a rooster) thwarted her wedding to Shiva coming from Shuchindram, so she remained a virgin and continued penance. Tradition attributes consecration to sage Parasurama; the blue-stone idol faces east, famed for its radiant nose ring. (VERIFY: sources disagree on Shakti Peetha count — 51, 52 and 108 claimed; '3000 years' age is traditional, not archaeological. Opening hours differ across sources. Coordinates from geocoder place the temple ~0.2 km inland from the shoreline — minor uncertainty.)

name: Kumari Amman Temple
town_description: Kanyakumari is the town at the southernmost tip of mainland India, in Kanyakumari district of Tamil Nadu, where the Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean meet at the Triveni Sangam. A historic pilgrimage centre since at least the 1st century CE, it draws devotees to the Kumari Amman temple and tourists for its sunrise/sunset views, the Vivekananda Rock Memorial and the Thiruvalluvar statue.

travel.airport: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport, about 100 km (verify exact distance)
travel.road: On NH 44; connected by bus to Nagercoil (22 km), Madurai (245 km) and other Tamil Nadu cities

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for weather; Navaratri (Sep-Oct) and Chitra Pournami (May) are the grandest festival times
visitor_information.opening_hours: Approx 4:30 AM-12:15 PM and 4:00-8:15 PM (VERIFY: sources vary — also reported 6:00-11:00 AM and 4:00-8:00 PM)
